content.text: {"grade": 5, "complete": false, "main_gap": "Lemma 4's acyclicity claim is false: |E|<|V| does not preclude cycles/loops, and the chosen component (containing vertex n) can contain a loop, breaking the |Xi| <= sum of slacks bound.", "errors": [{"description": "False graph-theoretic deduction in the lower bound (Lemma 4). A multigraph with |E|<|V| may well contain a cycle or loop (e.g. a triangle plus a disjoint edge on 5 vertices, 4 edges). The stated justification tacitly assumes the cycle spans all vertices. Repair is short (pick any component C with |E_C|<|V_C|, which must be a tree; (3.1) holds for any nonempty subset), but it is not the argument given.", "quote": "Since $|E|<|V|$, the multigraph $G$ contains no cycle and no loop: a cycle or a loop through $v$ vertices already uses at least $v$ edges, so a graph containing one would have at least as many edges as vertices, forcing $|E|\\ge|V|$ — impossible."}, {"description": "As a consequence, the specific component chosen (the one containing vertex n) need not be loopless/bipartite. Concretely, for n=2 with pieces 4/7,2/7,1/7 and Y cutting 4/7 into 0.2,0.2,0.1714, the pairs are {2/7,0.2} and {0.2,0.1714}: the latter is a loop at the largest piece, and the term s(pi)a+s(pi)a' is then a sum, not a difference, so the final chain u<=|Xi|<=sum eps_i fails.", "quote": "let $T=(V_T,E_T)$ be the component containing the vertex $n$ (the longest original piece), a simple tree (possibly a single vertex)."}], "notes": "Correct answer; Lemmas 1, 2, 3 and the whole upper bound (Lemma 5, subset-sum gap plus cross-pairing construction) are carefully and correctly done. Only the acyclicity step of the lower bound is erroneous, though repairable in one line."}
